name: Civil unrest
summary: Fifth weekend of cost-of-living protests in France on 14 Nov; at least 10 killed in Guinea mining clashes on 12–13 Nov
state: France saw a fifth straight Saturday of nationwide cost-of-living protests on 14 Nov, with about 106,000 marchers by the interior ministry's count and 200,000 by union count; no deaths were reported (Malay Mail, citing AFP). In Guinea, the government said at least 10 people were killed and 13 injured in clashes between protesters and security forces in Siguiri over a ban on artisanal gold mining (Al Jazeera, 13 Nov). Sustained protests and localised deadly unrest keep Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest in a major country was found as of 17 Nov.
for_you: Travellers to France may meet weekend marches and transport disruption in Paris and other cities; FCDO travel advice lists current local guidance. Turnout in France has been easing since early November.
rubric_hit: Significant protests in several countries and deadly unrest in one (Guinea, 10 killed) meet Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest

sources.title: More than 100,000 march across France as protests enter fifth weekend
At least 10 killed in Guinea clashes over gold mining ban

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
